page.layout: One page of text, with marginal section numbers in the right margin. Running head at top: page number left, running title right. Main text in one column, from the head "XV." down to the first thesis "I." of XXVII. Catchword at the bottom right.

main_text.p: XV. Elocutio est, quâ res convenienti stilo ornatur. Quò pertinent tropus, figura, & copia. Tropus est venusta vocis commutatio. Figura est venusta habitus orationis commutatio. Estque dictionis, vel sententiæ.5 Illa colorem & gratiam, hæc vehementiam & affectum conciliat orationi. Copia est, quâ oratio amplitudinem & magnificentiam aliquam consequitur. Estq; verborum, vel rerum. Copia verborum consistit in synonymis, epithetis, & variatione sententiæ grammaticâ, rhetoricâ & logicâ.10 Copia rerum consistit in aptâ diuisione materiæ, & singularum partium deductione ex locis inuentionis Logicæ. Exempla elocutionis sunt in toto Scripturæ corpore. Stilus namque Scripturæ non est nisi eloquentissimus, idque hanc ob causam, quòd ἡ ἀφέλεια ἡ πρὸς τὸ ἁπλ-15 τὸν, h.e. simplicitas & superfluitatis neglectus, veritatis colorem ita conci-ant[?] fermoni Spiritus sancti, vt omnem diligentiam omnemque artem aliorum scriptorum longè superet.

XVI. Memoria est vis animi, quâ orator rem cognitam, sæpeque repetitam probè meminit. Dico rem cognitam; quia requiritur omnium primò rerum memorandarum intellectio. Addo, sæpe repetitam: quia hoc vno artificio imaginatio, memoria, affectus, totusque adeo homo veluti repletur. Vide Mnemonicam infra.20
XVII. Pronuntiatio est, quâ orator orationem suam aptè enuntiat. Voce scil. clarâ, distinctâ, firmâ, mediocri, æquabili, variâ: & gestu, qui vocem subsequitur, & animo paret unâ cum voce.
main_text.head: XXVII. POETICA SACRA.
main_text.p: I. Poëtica sacra est ars efficiendi poëma ad imitationem Scripturæ.25

page.notes: The marginal numerals (5, 10, 15, 20, 25) are read from their placement every five lines and are approximate; the margin marks beside "rhetoricâ" and "ad" may be different numbers. The Greek phrase "ἡ ἀφέλεια ἡ πρὸς τὸ ἁπλ-" / "τὸν" and the word "conci-ant" are doubtful. The bottom-right mark "II.Poë" was read as a catchword "Poë" with the "II." possibly a signature; this is uncertain. The "II." at the very bottom was transcribed as a footer and may not belong to the main text. "Vocefcil." was read as "Voce scil." (scilicet).
